title: A Semantic/Net-Centric Approach for Sustainable Cities
content: This paper introduces a semantic-network approach to urban transformation, focusing on the development of a framework that integrates geospatial and network data into a Sustainable City Ontology Model. The research begins by extracting data from OpenStreetMap (OSM) files, generating dataframes, maps, and graphs for statistical, geospatial, and network analysis. Then, the Sustainable City Ontology Model is developed and populated with this data and metadata. The ontology enables semantic analysis through reasoning, ontology-based network analysis, and SPARQL queries, facilitating the exploration of emerging urban patterns and planning models. In addition to developing the semantic framework, this paper discusses the potential of network theory in guiding the digital and green transitions in city planning and proposes a conceptual methodology for the future creation of network-based sustainability indices, which will be explored in subsequent research. Future work will focus on uploading the ontology to a linked open data cloud, developing an API for user-friendly querying, and advancing the development of network-based sustainability metrics. This framework lays the foundation for transforming urban ecosystems, fostering resilience, and supporting cities in navigating the twin transitions of sustainability and digitalization.
